description: We are curious minds passionate about space, science, creativity and storytelling. Our project brings the stories of forgotten space hardware to life through an illustrated book filled with mystery and discovery. We welcome enthusiastic collaborators skilled in research, writing, illustration, graphic design and visual storytelling. Curiosity, creativity and teamwork are what matter most. Join us in exploring the stories beyond the stars!
summary:
The Starbound Archive is an illustrated educational book that brings attention to lesser-known, unsuccessful, abandoned, and lost NASA space missions. While the history of space exploration often celebrates groundbreaking achievements, many missions that faced technical failures or never reached their intended destinations remain relatively unknown.

This project aims to uncover these overlooked stories and present them through engaging, first-person narratives in which each spacecraft recounts its purpose, journey, challenges, and eventual fate. Missions such as Genesis, Ranger 3, and CONTOUR demonstrate that even when a mission does not achieve its original objective, it can still contribute valuable scientific knowledge and engineering lessons.

Combining historical research, scientific explanations, creative storytelling, and detailed digital illustrations, the book makes the complex history of space exploration accessible and engaging for young readers and space enthusiasts.

The project's central message is that failure is not the absence of achievement. Every mission represents human curiosity, innovation, and the courage to explore the unknown.

The Starbound Archive seeks to preserve these overlooked chapters of NASA's history and remind readers that every journey into space has something to teach humanity.
details:
The Starbound Archive is an illustrated educational book dedicated to uncovering the forgotten stories of unsuccessful, abandoned, and lesser-known NASA space missions.

While space exploration is often remembered through its greatest achievements, numerous missions that faced technical failures, lost contact, or never reached their intended destinations remain overlooked. This project brings these stories back into focus, exploring the ambitions, challenges, unexpected outcomes, and scientific contributions behind them.

Through creative first-person narratives, each spacecraft becomes the storyteller of its own journey. Readers discover why the mission was designed, what it hoped to achieve, what went wrong, and what humanity learned from its experience. The book combines historical research, accessible scientific explanations, and detailed digital illustrations to make these stories engaging for young readers and space enthusiasts.

Beginning with missions such as Genesis, Ranger 3, and CONTOUR, the archive highlights an important distinction: not every unsuccessful mission is without scientific value. Some leave behind discoveries, engineering lessons, and knowledge that help shape future exploration.

Our goal is to make overlooked space history accessible, inspire curiosity about science and engineering, and celebrate the spirit of exploration even when missions do not go according to plan.

The Starbound Archive believes that every mission has a story, every setback has a lesson, and every journey deserves to be remembered.
